x=tan(t): x/(1+sqrt(1+x^2)) = tan(t)/(1+sec t) = sin t/(1+cos t) = tan(t/2), so the expression is (1/2)tan^-1(x); derivative 1/(2(1+x^2)). Note options A/B/D carry sqrt(1+x^2) in the denominator, which is the wrong shape.

tan^-1((x-1)/(x+1)) = tan^-1(x) - pi/4 for x>-1, so derivative = 1/(1+x^2). Direct check: u'=2/(x+1)^2 and 1/(1+u^2)=(x+1)^2/(2x^2+2), product = 2/(2x^2+2) = 1/(1+x^2). Options C/D (x^2+2x+2 = (x+1)^2+1) are the un-simplified-wrongly trap.

sqrt((1-x)/2) = sin(t/2) with x=cos t, so the expression is (1/2)cos^-1(x) and the derivative is -1/(2*sqrt(1-x^2)). All four options carry sqrt(x(2-x)) = sqrt(2x-x^2), which equals sqrt(1-x^2) ONLY at x=0.5 (checked x=0.3: 1-x^2=0.91 vs x(2-x)=0.51). Central-difference at x=0.5 gives -0.5774 = -1/(2*sqrt(0.75)), consistent with my form. Option A is the derivative of sin^-1(sqrt((2-x)/2)), so the stem's numerator was probably meant to be 2-x.

x*sin^-1(x) is EVEN (odd*odd), so the integral is 2*int_0^1. By parts: [x^2/2 * asin x]_0^1 - (1/2)int_0^1 x^2/sqrt(1-x^2) dx = pi/4 - (1/2)(pi/4) = pi/8. Doubled = pi/4. Cross-checked by x=sin t: (1/2)int_0^{pi/2} t sin2t dt = pi/8. Option A (0) is the 'assume odd, so zero' trap - the integrand is even, not odd. pi/4 is not offered.

x=tan(t): (sec t - 1)/tan t = (1-cos t)/sin t = tan(t/2), so the expression is (1/2)tan^-1(x) and the derivative is 1/(2(1+x^2)) - the SAME function as 05-15. Here every option has sqrt(1+x^2) in the denominator; 1/(2(1+x^2)) is absent, so no option matches. (05-15 does offer it as its option C.)

Domain [-1,1]. f(x)=2sin^-1(x)-tan^-1(x) has f'(x)=2/sqrt(1-x^2) - 1/(1+x^2) >= 2 - 1 > 0 on (-1,1), so f is strictly increasing and has at most one zero; f(0)=0. Endpoints confirm sign change (f(1)=pi-pi/4>0, f(-1)<0). Exactly 1.

tan^-1 x = x - x^3/3 + O(x^5); sin^-1 x = x + x^3/6 + O(x^5). Difference = -(1/3+1/6)x^3 = -x^3/2, so the limit is -1/2. Numeric at x=0.1: (0.0996687-0.1001674)/0.001 = -0.4987. Options only offer +-1/3 and +-1/6 (the two individual series coefficients), not their sum -1/2.
